record.paper_title: Open Questions On Nuclear Collective Motion
record.context_brief: Microscopic Bohr Hamiltonian beyond adiabatic beta vibrations
record.original_question: How can non-adiabatic coupling and fragmentation be incorporated into microscopic Bohr-Hamiltonian descriptions derived from nuclear mean-field methods so that predicted beta-vibrational or shape-coexistence 0+ states, especially in well-deformed nuclei such as 166Er and 178Hf, do not remain artificially too vibrational or systematically too high in energy?

evidence.quote: It needs to be underlined that the restriction to the zero quasiparticle solutions in the GCM and the use of of the GAO implicitly introduce an adiabatic approximation.
The theory gives a good qualitative account of the range of variation of the excitation energy of the first excited 0+ state, but the predicted energies are systematically 50% high.
In addition they observe that the 0+2 states are generally too vibrational. The discrepancy is particularly precarious for well deformed nuclei.

For example, the 0+2 states in 166Er and 178Hf do not show the enhanced E2 transition probability expected for a β vibration, which is predicted by the BH. Instead some collective enhancement for transitions from higher 0+ states is observed, which indicates the fragmentation or absence of the collective β vibration [6, 7].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the microscopic Bohr Hamiltonian formalism for nuclear collective quadrupole motion, in which a five-dimensional collective Schrödinger equation in the shape variables (β, γ) and three Euler angles is derived from a self-consistent mean-field theory (e.g., Hartree–Fock–Bogoliubov with a chosen effective interaction) by means of the generator coordinate method (GCM) together with the Gaussian overlap approximation (GOA). Restricting the GCM to zero-quasiparticle generator states and using the GOA effectively imposes an adiabatic approximation: the collective coordinates are decoupled from non-collective (quasiparticle) degrees of freedom, and the resulting Bohr Hamiltonian has the form

  H_coll = T_vib(β,γ) + T_rot(β,γ; Î) + V(β,γ),

with mass parameters and potential V(β,γ) computed microscopically from the mean-field configurations.

When applied to even–even deformed nuclei, this adiabatic microscopic Bohr Hamiltonian systematically predicts excited 0⁺ states (interpreted as β-vibrations or shape-coexisting states) whose excitation energies are too high (typically by about 50%) and whose character is too vibrational. In particular, for the well-deformed nuclei ¹⁶⁶Er and ¹⁷⁸Hf, experiment shows that the lowest excited 0⁺ state does not carry the enhanced E2 transition strength to the ground-state band predicted for a collective β-vibration; instead, collective E2 strength is fragmented over higher-lying 0⁺ states.

Problem. Formulate an extension of the microscopic Bohr Hamiltonian, derived from a nuclear mean-field/EDF starting point, that explicitly incorporates (i) non-adiabatic coupling between the collective quadrupole coordinates (β, γ) and two-quasiparticle (or higher) intrinsic excitations, and (ii) the resulting fragmentation of collective β-vibrational strength among several 0⁺ states. The extension should be such that, when applied to ¹⁶⁶Er and ¹⁷⁸Hf, the predicted spectrum of low-lying 0⁺ states and the distribution of their B(E2; 0⁺ → 2⁺_g) strengths reproduce the experimentally observed pattern—namely, the lowest excited 0⁺ state is not artificially enhanced as a pure β-vibration, the collective E2 strength is fragmented over higher 0⁺ states, and the systematic ~50% overestimation of excitation energies is removed. Specify the additional dynamical variables, coupling operators, and approximation scheme (beyond zero-quasiparticle GCM + GOA) required to achieve this.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and microscopic-Bohr-Hamiltonian studies (e.g., the five-dimensional collective Hamiltonian derived from EDF mean fields via GCM+GOA) continue to identify the adiabatic restriction to zero-quasiparticle generator states as a known limitation, and the character of low-lying 0⁺ "β-vibrational" states in well-deformed rare-earth nuclei is described as unresolved. No published framework appears to deliver a fully microscopic, non-adiabatic extension that simultaneously corrects the systematic overestimation of excited 0⁺ energies and reproduces the observed fragmentation of E2 strength in ¹⁶⁶Er and ¹⁷⁸Hf, so the question is best classified as still open.

status_evidence.title: Quadrupole collective states within the Bohr collective Hamiltonian
status_evidence.snippet: Microscopic derivation of the collective quadrupole Bohr Hamiltonian applied to even–even nuclei; discusses limitations of the adiabatic approximation.
status_evidence.claim: The standard microscopic Bohr Hamiltonian rests on an adiabatic GCM+GOA framework whose limitations for excited 0⁺ states are acknowledged.

status_evidence.title: Microscopic derivation of the Bohr–Mottelson collective Hamiltonian
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews five-dimensional collective Schrödinger equation derived from time evolution of self-consistent mean field; notes β-vibrational bands remain mysterious and require radical review.
status_evidence.claim: The microscopic understanding of β-vibrational 0⁺ states in deformed nuclei is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: Microscopic Version of the Bohr-Mottelson Model and Its Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Applications of the microscopic Bohr–Mottelson model to deformed nuclei discuss persistent discrepancies for excited 0⁺ states.
status_evidence.claim: Discrepancies in 0⁺ energies and E2 strengths persist in microscopic Bohr-model applications.
